screen: `DAY EIGHT-HUNDRED-SIX.`

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Yaksha's questions reached four big ones: the happy one at home, the path the great have walked, time's cooking pot, and the wonder that we live as if we never die. Your line was a modest supper under your own roof. Did you eat one meal slowly? Day eight hundred six.
screen: `THE YAKSHA'S QUESTIONS.` · `WHAT IS WONDERFUL.`

segments.voice: The questions are over, and the yaksha is satisfied. One of your brothers may live, he says. Choose. On the shore lie four of them. Bhima, whose strength the family leans on. Arjuna, the archer they'll need in any war to come. And the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva. Yudhishthira looks at them all, one by one, for a long moment. Then he names one, and the yaksha, puzzled, asks him why.
screen: `ONE BROTHER MAY LIVE.` → `FOUR ON THE SHORE.` → `CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: Let Nakula live, Yudhishthira says. Why him? the yaksha asks. Why not Bhima, so strong, or Arjuna, whom you all depend on? Yudhishthira's answer is about fairness. My father had two wives, Kunti and Madri. I am Kunti's son, and I'm alive. Let Madri have a living son too. That's why Nakula. He passes over the brothers who could win him a war, and chooses the one who keeps the family fair. The yaksha is delighted. Because you hold harmlessness higher than gain or pleasure, he says, let all four of your brothers live. And they stand up, as if from sleep, with their thirst gone. Then the stranger shows his face. He is Dharma himself, Yudhishthira's own father. He came to see his son, and to test him. The deer that ran off with the fire-sticks was Dharma too. So the whole day, the chase, the thirst, the lake, the questions, was a father asking his son: do you know what dharma asks of you? Dharma offers him gifts. Yudhishthira asks first for the brahmin's fire-sticks back, the errand that started it all. Then that in the coming year in hiding, no one will recognize the brothers. And he asks to conquer greed, anger and folly, and to keep his mind on generosity, truth and self-discipline. Dharma grants it all. The Pandavas walk back to their camp with the fire-sticks in hand. And waiting ahead is a year in disguise.
screen: `LET NAKULA LIVE.` · `A LIVING SON FOR MADRI TOO.` · `THE YAKSHA IS DHARMA, HIS FATHER.` · then, large: `ALL FOUR STAND UP.`

807.title: Virata: the year in disguise
807.hook: the forest years are over, and Yudhishthira asks each brother and Draupadi a plain question: what will you be?
807.carry: every disguise is built from something real
807.howItsDone: The Virata book is read and retold as part of the Mahabharata, and the disguises the Pandavas choose (Kanka, Vallava, Brihannala, Sairandhri) are familiar names from retellings and performances of the epic.

screen: `DAY EIGHT-HUNDRED-SEVEN.`

segments.voice: Yesterday the Yaksha's questions came to an end, and the voice at the lake showed itself as Dharma. Your line was the one who keeps the family fair. Like Yudhishthira choosing Nakula, did you think first of the side with no one speaking for it? Day eight hundred seven.
screen: `THE YAKSHA'S QUESTIONS.` · `THE VOICE WAS DHARMA.`

segments.voice: The forest is behind them now, and a harder stretch of the exile is ahead. The terms of the dice game were plain: one last year lived among people, without being recognized. If anyone sees through them, the exile begins again. So the five brothers and Draupadi sit together, and Yudhishthira asks each of them a question. Not where will you hide. What will you be? Where will you work, and as whom? They have chosen a kingdom to vanish into: the land of the Matsyas, ruled by King Virata. Today the Virata book opens with something close to a job interview, held in secret.
screen: `ONE YEAR, UNRECOGNIZED.` → `WHAT WILL YOU BE?` → `THE COURT OF KING VIRATA.`

segments.voice: Listen to the answers, because each one tells you something. Yudhishthira goes first. He will be Kanka, a Brahmin who plays dice with the king and keeps him company. Stop on that. The man whose love of dice cost them everything chooses dice as his cover. Bhima will be Vallava, the cook, and he'll wrestle if the court wants a show. The brother with the famous appetite will run the kitchen. Arjuna has a harder problem: the scars a bowstring leaves on a warrior's arms. He'll hide them under bangles and live as Brihannala, a eunuch who teaches singing and dance to the women of the palace. Nakula will keep the king's horses. Sahadeva will keep the cattle. And Draupadi, a queen, will serve the queen as Sairandhri, a maid who dresses hair. Notice what none of them does. Nobody pretends to a skill they don't have. Every disguise is built from something real. The rank is hidden. The person isn't. Then their priest, Dhaumya, gives them advice for life in a king's house, and it reads like advice for a first week at any new job. Don't take a seat that might belong to someone else. Speak when you're asked. Don't show off, and don't gossip about the king's private affairs. Be useful, and be quiet about it. The great heroes of the epic are about to spend a year as staff.
screen: `EACH ONE ASKED: WHAT WILL YOU BE?` · `THE DICE MAN CHOOSES DICE` · `EVERY DISGUISE BUILT ON A REAL SKILL` · then, large: `DHAUMYA: HOW TO LIVE AT COURT`

808.title: Virata: the year in disguise
808.hook: a bundle tied high in a shami tree near the cremation ground, and nobody wants to go near it

screen: `DAY EIGHT-HUNDRED-EIGHT.`

segments.voice: Yesterday each of them answered the question: what will you be? Kanka, Vallava, Brihannala, Sairandhri. Your line was every disguise is built from something real. Which real skill did you notice under one of your roles? Day eight hundred eight.
screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `EVERY DISGUISE BUILT ON A REAL SKILL.`

segments.voice: A shami tree stands near a cremation ground outside King Virata's city. Thick branches, hard to climb, and a place people would rather walk past. Nakula climbs it. He ties a long bundle high in the branches, wrapped tight so the rain won't reach it. Inside is luggage that could end the whole disguise: Arjuna's bow, the Gandiva, and the brothers' other weapons. A wandering cook can't carry a bow every warrior knows on sight. So the weapons have to stay behind. Today, how the Pandavas walk into Virata's city with nothing that could give them away.
screen: `A SHAMI TREE BY THE CREMATION GROUND.` → `NAKULA CLIMBS.` → `THE WEAPONS STAY BEHIND.`

segments.voice: The text adds a detail that's half clever, half grim. To keep curious people away, the brothers tie a dead body to the tree as well, and they tell passing herdsmen it's an old family custom, a mother's body hung there by tradition. Nobody climbs a tree like that. The bundle will wait. Then they enter the city one at a time, so no one sees five strong men arrive together. Yudhishthira comes first, with dice wrapped in cloth under his arm, and King Virata takes to him at once and makes him his companion. Bhima arrives with a cook's ladle and a knife. Arjuna comes in women's ornaments and asks to teach dance. Nakula and Sahadeva go to the stables and the herds. Draupadi walks the streets in a single worn cloth until Queen Sudeshna sees her from a terrace and calls her up. The queen hesitates. You're too beautiful, she says, the king will look at you. Draupadi answers with a story of her own: she has husbands, Gandharvas, heavenly beings who guard her unseen and will punish anyone who troubles her. It's a disguise inside the disguise, and it's also true. Her husbands really are watching over her, from the kitchen, the stables and the dice table. The heroes leave their weapons in a tree and their names at the gate, and keep only themselves.
screen: `A BODY TO KEEP PEOPLE AWAY` · `ARRIVING ONE AT A TIME` · `THE QUEEN'S WORRY` · then, large: `HIDDEN GANDHARVA HUSBANDS`

809.hook: Kichaka kicks Sairandhri in front of the king, and the man at the dice table tells her to go inside
809.carry: once again she's the one who speaks
809.howItsDone: The Kichaka episode is retold and staged in Indian performance traditions, and readers of the epic discuss Yudhishthira's restraint and Draupadi's protest side by side.

screen: `DAY EIGHT-HUNDRED-NINE.`

segments.voice: Yesterday the weapons went up into the shami tree, and the Pandavas walked into Virata's city one at a time. Your line was keep only themselves. What did you notice when you set something down? Day eight hundred nine.
screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `THE WEAPONS IN THE SHAMI TREE.`

segments.voice: The disguises have held for months. Then the queen's brother comes to visit. His name is Kichaka. He commands King Virata's army, and the court is a little afraid of him. He sees the maid Sairandhri and wants her. She refuses him, plainly, and tells him she's protected. He doesn't care. He goes to his sister, the queen, and the queen sends Sairandhri to his house on an errand, to fetch wine. Draupadi knows exactly what this errand is. Today, a different kind of disguise: the one where you have to stand still and watch.
screen: `THE QUEEN'S BROTHER, KICHAKA.` → `SHE REFUSES HIM.` → `AN ERRAND THAT IS A TRAP.`

segments.voice: At Kichaka's house he grabs at her. She breaks free and runs, straight into the royal court, where King Virata sits, with Kanka beside him at the dice. Kichaka chases her in, catches her by the hair, and kicks her to the floor in front of everyone. And here the epic does something painful. It shows us the brothers. Bhima is there, and his face darkens, and he stares at a big tree as if he means to tear it up and use it as a club. Yudhishthira sees it. Quietly, in his role as Kanka, he presses Bhima's toe and says something like: looking for firewood, cook? Go cut your trees somewhere else. But Draupadi doesn't stay quiet. From the floor she speaks to the king, in his own court. What kind of king, she asks, lets a woman be struck in front of him and does nothing? Is this how justice works in the Matsya court? A queen once dragged into one assembly hall is struck in another, and once again she's the one who speaks. Then Kanka turns to her. Go to the queen's rooms, he tells her. Your Gandharva husbands will act when the time is right. You're interrupting the king's game. It sounds cold. It's meant to. One word of recognition and the whole year is lost. The disguise holds. But the epic makes sure we feel what it costs, and who pays.
screen: `A CHASE INTO THE COURT` · `BHIMA STARES AT A TREE` · `DRAUPADI SPEAKS TO THE KING` · then, large: `KANKA: GO INSIDE, NOT NOW`

screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `KANKA: GO INSIDE, NOT NOW.`

segments.voice: It's night in King Virata's palace. Draupadi can't sleep. She gets up, crosses the dark courtyard, and goes to the kitchen, where the royal cook Vallava is asleep. She doesn't go to Yudhishthira. She goes to Bhima. She wakes him, and the first thing she says is a question: how can you sleep? Today, a conversation in a kitchen at night, and a plan that changes the rest of the year.
screen: `NIGHT IN THE PALACE.` → `SHE GOES TO THE KITCHEN.` → `HOW CAN YOU SLEEP?`

segments.voice: Then she tells him all of it, and the epic gives her room to speak at length. Not only Kichaka. The whole long road: the dice hall, the forest, a queen now serving another queen, grinding sandal paste until her hands are rough. She looks at what her husbands have become, too: the king of the world playing dice for a living, the great archer teaching dance with braided hair. She isn't only angry. She's grieving for all of them. And Bhima listens. The text says he holds her hands and weeps with her. Then the cook makes a plan. Tell Kichaka yes, he says. Tell him to meet you tonight in the dancing hall, the room where the princesses learn dance by day and that stands empty after dark. I'll be waiting there instead. So Draupadi does it. Kichaka arrives in the dark, dressed for a meeting, and finds the cook. They fight, two strong men in an empty hall, and Bhima kills him. In the morning, the court finds Kichaka dead, and they decide the hidden Gandharvas must have done it. Kichaka's kinsmen try to take revenge on Sairandhri, and Bhima rescues her from them too. Here's what to notice. Even now, nobody names the cook. The town is frightened of the maid and her invisible husbands. The disguise bends, and it holds. Draupadi went to the brother who would act, and he listened first, and the night ends with the year still safe.

segments.voice: Cattle raiders. The Kauravas have heard that Kichaka is dead, and they come for King Virata's herds. The king has already ridden out to fight raiders on another side, taking Kanka, the cook and the herdsmen with him. At home, among the women of the palace, sits his young son, Prince Uttara. And Uttara talks big. If I only had a charioteer, he says, I'd beat the whole Kuru army. They'd look at me and wonder if I was Arjuna himself. The person he's talking about is standing a few feet away, in bangles. Today, a frightened prince, a dance teacher, and a ride back to the shami tree.
screen: `THE KAURAVAS RAID THE HERDS.` → `UTTARA'S BOAST.` → `ARJUNA IS IN THE ROOM.`

segments.voice: Sairandhri speaks up. Brihannala, she says, once drove a chariot for Arjuna. Uttara is embarrassed to take a dance teacher to war, but he has no one else. The teacher fumbles with the armor on purpose, putting it on wrong, and the palace women laugh. The princesses ask for fine cloths from the beaten Kurus for their dolls. Then the chariot rolls out, and Uttara sees the army: the banners, the elephants, the great warriors of the Kuru house, Bhishma, Drona, Karna. His boast falls apart. He jumps from the chariot and runs. And Brihannala runs after him. Long braid flying, robes swirling, across the field, and some of the Kuru soldiers watching think: that runs like a man, that runs like Arjuna. The teacher catches the prince, not to shame him, but to steady him. Don't be afraid, he says, in effect. You drive. I'll fight. Then they turn the chariot to the shami tree by the cremation ground. Uttara climbs up, unwraps the bundle, and finds weapons no dance teacher should own, the great bow Gandiva among them. Whose are these? he asks. And Brihannala tells him the truth. I am Arjuna. Notice who hears it first. Not a king, not an enemy. A scared boy who just ran away, and who is now trusted to hold the reins.

812.title: Virata: the year in disguise
812.hook: the year ends the way it began, with dice, and then the five servants of Virata's court take the royal seats
812.tomorrow: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
812.howItsDone: The Virata book closes with the Pandavas revealed and the marriage of Princess Uttara to Abhimanyu, and retellings pause on Arjuna's refusal to marry the student he taught.

screen: `DAY EIGHT-HUNDRED-TWELVE.`

segments.voice: Yesterday a frightened prince ran, a dance teacher ran after him, and at the shami tree Brihannala said: I am Arjuna. Your line was I am Arjuna. Did you steady anyone today? Day eight hundred twelve.
screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `I AM ARJUNA.`

segments.voice: A conch sounds across the field, and the Kuru warriors know that sound. Arjuna is back. He fights the whole raiding army with Uttara at the reins, and in the end he uses a weapon that makes the Kuru warriors fall into a stupor. He sends Uttara among them to take their fine upper cloths, for the princesses' dolls, as promised. The cattle go home. So does a prince who ran away that morning. Today, the last day of the Virata story, and the masks come off.
screen: `A CONCH THE KURUS KNOW.` → `CLOTHS FOR THE DOLLS.` → `THE LAST DAY OF THE MASKS.`

segments.voice: Back at the palace, King Virata is overjoyed. My son has beaten the Kurus! He sits down to dice with Kanka to celebrate, and keeps praising Uttara. Kanka says quietly: with Brihannala driving, how could he lose? Virata is offended. He keeps praising his son; Kanka keeps naming the dance teacher. And the king, angry, throws the dice in Kanka's face. Blood runs from Yudhishthira's nose. Sairandhri is there in a moment, catching the drops in a vessel before they reach the floor. Brihannala is kept outside the door, because Arjuna has sworn that whoever draws his brother's blood outside of battle will not live. Look at how this year closes. It began with dice, a king hiding as a dice player. It ends with dice, and the hidden king bleeding, and still not saying who he is. Then, with the year behind them, the brothers walk into the court in royal clothes and sit on the royal seats, and Virata is furious until Arjuna tells him who they are. The king is stunned. He offers his daughter, Princess Uttara, to Arjuna as a bride. And Arjuna says no. I was her teacher, he says, and she trusted me as a daughter trusts a father. Let her marry my son, Abhimanyu. The teacher stays a teacher, even after the mask comes off. And so the Virata story closes: the disguises, the shami tree, Kichaka, the dancing hall, the frightened prince, and today, the masks set down.
screen: `VIRATA PRAISES HIS SON` · `VIRATA'S DICE STRIKE KANKA` · `THE MASKS COME OFF` · then, large: `A TEACHER, NOT A HUSBAND`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably, and cup your hands loosely in your lap, the way Sairandhri holds the vessel under Kanka's face. Bring to mind one small act of care someone did for you without a word, one nobody praised. Breathing in, let it come back clearly. Breathing out, let your cupped hands hold it for a moment. Stay with it for a few breaths. If you pray, you can hold that person in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Virata. The king who struck his own dice partner, and learned soon after that he had been hosting the Pandavas all year.
screen: `VIRATA — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the teacher stays a teacher. Today, give credit where it's really due, the way Kanka named Brihannala, even when it costs you. Day eight hundred twelve.

screen: `DAY 812 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: UDYOGA: THE EMBASSY, KRISHNA'S COUNSEL, KARNA AND KUNTI.`
